sections.title: What you know
sections.content: You know the *-ra* and *-se* endings from B2 Unit 15, and you met *hubiese* in the first lesson of this unit. *Hubiese* + participle means exactly the same as *hubiera* + participle in every use you have learned: after *si*, after *ojalá* and after *que*.

sections.title: The same sentence, two forms
rows: Si lo hubiera sabido, habría venido.
If I had known, I would have come.
Si lo hubiese sabido, habría venido.
I did not think they had finished.

sections.title: Which one will you meet?
sections.content: In Latin America people say and write *hubiera* almost always. *Hubiese* is the form you will meet in older books, in formal documents and in some careful writing, and a writer may use both in one text. You only need to recognise it, and in this course an answer with either form is accepted. If you decide to write *hubiese*, keep it for the whole text.

items.spanish: Aunque nadie lo hubiese dicho antes, todos lo sabían.
items.english: Although nobody had said it before, everyone knew it.

items.spanish: Si hubiésemos sabido la verdad, habríamos actuado de otra manera.
items.english: If we had known the truth, we would have acted differently.

items.spanish: Ojalá hubiese leído ese prólogo antes.
items.english: I wish I had read that preface before.

sections.content: Do not read *hubiese* as another tense or a more distant past. It is *hubiera* in a more formal dress. Watch the accent in the *nosotros* form: *hubiésemos*.
